# Manas Majhi — Full Essay Index

> Complete listing of all 223 published essays at manasmajhi.com.
> Each entry: URL · title · date · excerpt.
> For site overview and author biography, see https://www.manasmajhi.com/llms.txt

## Opportunity (19 essays)

- [What Missed Opportunity Actually Costs](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/what-missed-opportunity-costs) — 2026-03-21
  The cost of a blocked path is not just borne by the person it blocks. The world pays too — in the things that never get built, the problems that stay unsolved, the potential that never compounds.

- [The Obligation That Comes With Getting Through the Door](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/the-obligation-that-comes-with-getting-through-the-door) — 2026-03-05
  When you are the first person from your background to reach a certain room, you carry something that wasn't handed to you. What you do with it is a choice — and it matters more than most people acknowledge.

- [The Information Gap](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/the-information-gap) — 2026-01-20
  Most opportunity doesn't fail because it doesn't exist. It fails because the people who need it most don't know it's there. Information is the invisible infrastructure of opportunity.

- [The Geography of Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/the-geography-of-opportunity) — 2025-12-30
  Where you are born is still the single most powerful predictor of what becomes available to you. Not because of difference — because of distribution.

- [AI and Opportunity — Distribution or Concentration?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/ai-and-opportunity) — 2025-11-23
  The optimistic case for AI is that it distributes opportunity by making powerful tools accessible to everyone. The pessimistic case is that it concentrates opportunity by accelerating the advantage of those who already have it. Both are happening. The question is which one is winning.

- [Networks Are Not Networking](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/networks-are-not-networking) — 2025-11-15
  The network you were born into is not something you built. It's something you inherited. For first-generation professionals, understanding this distinction changes everything about how you navigate the world.

- [What Is Opportunity?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/what-is-opportunity) — 2025-06-08
  Not luck. Not access. Not advantage. Opportunity is a condition — the coincidence of capability, information, and the absence of a blocking constraint. Understanding what it actually is changes how you design systems to create more of it.

- [How Opportunity Compounds Over Time](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/how-opportunity-compounds) — 2025-06-01
  Opportunity does not arrive and depart in single moments. It accumulates — or it doesn't. The same mechanism that builds generational advantage also builds generational disadvantage. Understanding the compounding effect changes what interventions actually matter.

- [Opportunity in Rural India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/opportunity-in-rural-india) — 2025-05-25
  Rural India is not a single place. It is several hundred thousand distinct places, with different geographies, different crops, different castes, different distances from the nearest town with a decent school. The opportunity problem is as varied as the terrain.

- [Systems That Create Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/systems-that-create-opportunity) — 2025-05-18
  Opportunity doesn't appear randomly. It is the output of specific systems — some public, some private, some informal — that create the conditions under which capability connects to possibility. Understanding what those systems are and how they work is the starting point for building more of them.

- [Systems That Destroy Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/systems-that-destroy-opportunity) — 2025-05-11
  Opportunity doesn't only fail to form — it gets actively destroyed. The mechanisms are specific and mostly structural: credentialism that blocks by requirement rather than relevance, discrimination that reroutes by identity, extractive institutions that take rather than build. Understanding them is the first step to dismantling them.

- [How to Create Opportunity for Others](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/how-to-create-opportunity-for-others) — 2025-05-04
  There is a version of success that is purely personal — built on your own capability, captured for yourself, spent on your own life. And there is a version that compounds outward. The difference is not generosity. It is whether you understand what actually moved the needle for you.

- [Opportunity Changes Lives](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/opportunity-changes-lives) — 2025-02-12
  The mechanism by which opportunity changes a life is simple and well understood. The mystery is not how it works — it's why every system we've built to distribute it reliably does the opposite of what it claims to do.

- [Opportunity in India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/opportunity-in-india) — 2024-11-03
  India is not a uniform opportunity landscape. It is a country of extraordinary concentration alongside extraordinary absence — where the same decade produces world-class engineers and districts with no functional schools. Understanding that distribution is the beginning of understanding what opportunity in India actually means.

- [First-Generation Professionals and Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/first-generation-professionals-and-opportunity) — 2024-10-27
  Being the first in your family to enter a profession is not just a personal milestone. It is a specific structural position that comes with specific advantages and specific disadvantages that most people in that position don't have language for until years later.

- [Opportunity Gaps — Where They Exist and Why](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/opportunity-gaps) — 2024-10-20
  Opportunity gaps are not random and they are not primarily caused by individual failure. They cluster because systems create them predictably — and the interventions aimed at closing them keep failing because they address the symptom rather than the structure.

- [Talent Is Evenly Distributed. Opportunity Is Not.](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/talent-is-evenly-distributed) — 2023-12-19
  Talent is distributed by biology. Opportunity is distributed by geography, networks, and timing. The gap between them is not a talent problem — it is a systems problem. And it has specific, tractable solutions that most institutions aren't building.

- [Improving Lives With New Opportunities](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/improving-lives-with-new-opportunities) — 2023-11-23
  The talent gap is largely fictional. The opportunity gap is real — and it compounds in ways most systemic interventions don't account for, because they solve for access without solving for what makes access convert into outcomes.

- [Opportunity and Mobility in Modern India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/opportunity/opportunity-and-mobility-in-modern-india) — 2023-01-05
  Growth that people cannot participate in is not development. India is learning this distinction in real time.

## India (23 essays)

- [AI Adoption in Rural India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/ai-adoption-rural-india) — 2026-07-04
  India's AI story is being written in Bengaluru and Mumbai. The more important story — the one that determines whether AI expands or concentrates opportunity in India — is being written in the districts that the first wave of technology only partially reached.

- [What Global Employers Get Wrong About Indian Talent](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/what-global-employers-get-wrong-about-indian-talent) — 2026-06-16
  The credential read and the capability read are two separate exercises. After five years of placing Indian executives in global roles, I know which one most hiring processes skip.

- [Why Global Companies Should Hire From India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/why-global-companies-should-hire-from-india) — 2025-06-15
  India produces more engineering graduates per year than the US has engineers in total. That is not a staffing opportunity. It is a structural shift in where capability lives.

- [Nationalism vs Patriotism](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/nationalism-vs-patriotism) — 2025-06-11
  These two words are used interchangeably in Indian political discourse, and that confusion is doing real damage to how we think about love of country.

- [Why India's Moment Is Now](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/why-indias-moment-is-now) — 2025-04-27
  India has had inflection points before. This one is different — because for the first time, multiple structural advantages are converging simultaneously: demographic, digital, geopolitical, and institutional. The question is whether the execution matches the opportunity.

- [India's Technology Ecosystem](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-technology-ecosystem) — 2025-04-20
  India's technology story has three layers that are often conflated: the IT services legacy that built the industry, the consumer internet wave that created the unicorns, and the deep tech and SaaS wave that is now determining what comes next.

- [India's Startup Ecosystem](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-startup-ecosystem) — 2025-04-13
  India has produced over 100 unicorns and the third-largest startup ecosystem in the world. What that number obscures is more interesting than what it reveals: who is building, what they are building, and whether the infrastructure for the next generation is actually in place.

- [Remote Work and India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/remote-work-and-india) — 2025-03-30
  Remote work did not create India's talent export. It accelerated it — and changed the terms. The shift from outsourcing to remote employment is not just a pricing story. It is a structural change in how global talent flows.

- [India's Future in 10 Years](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-future-in-10-years) — 2025-03-23
  Projecting India's next decade requires holding two things simultaneously: genuine structural advantages that are real and compounding, and genuine execution risks that have derailed previous inflection points. Both are true. The outcome depends on which one wins.

- [Tier 2 and Tier 3 Cities in India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/tier-2-tier-3-cities-india) — 2025-03-16
  The next chapter of India's growth will be written in cities most outsiders have never heard of. Indore, Surat, Coimbatore, Vadodara, Vizag, Jaipur — these are not minor cities. They are places with real economies, real talent, and an underappreciated capacity to absorb the next wave of investment that the saturated metros cannot.

- [India's Infrastructure Revolution](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-infrastructure-revolution) — 2024-10-13
  India has built more infrastructure in the last decade than in the five decades before it combined. This is not a political claim — it is a measurable fact about roads, railways, ports, airports, and digital systems. What it means for the economy, and what is still missing, is the more interesting question.

- [The Most Underrated Innovation in India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/the-most-underrated-innovation-in-india) — 2024-10-01
  Everyone talks about the apps and the unicorns. The actually interesting stuff is the infrastructure underneath.

- [The India I See](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/the-india-i-see) — 2024-08-13
  Not the India of headlines or investor pitches. The one I have watched build itself in the in-between places.

- [The Future of Indian Cities](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/the-future-of-indian-cities) — 2024-07-22
  Indian cities are being shaped by decisions being made right now. The window to get them right is shorter than most people realize.

- [Digital Public Infrastructure](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/digital-public-infrastructure) — 2024-05-15
  India built something the rest of the world is still trying to understand: open, interoperable digital rails that no single company owns.

- [India's Greatest Asset Is Its People](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-greatest-asset-is-its-people) — 2024-04-24
  The demographic dividend is real. But dividends require investment — and India's human capital investment remains unequal.

- [India's AI Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/indias-ai-opportunity) — 2024-03-01
  India's AI advantage is not its volume of engineers. It is the combination of English-language capability, a domestic market large enough to stress-test at scale, and a cost structure that makes experimentation viable. Every country that becomes an AI power will need what India already has.

- [State Capacity Is the Ultimate Competitive Advantage](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/state-capacity-is-the-ultimate-competitive-advantage) — 2024-02-16
  Countries with high state capacity can absorb shocks, build infrastructure, and compound development in ways that low-capacity states simply cannot.

- [Building for a Billion People](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/building-for-a-billion-people) — 2023-12-27
  Scale at this magnitude is not just a bigger version of building for fewer people. It changes the problem entirely.

- [How 4G Changed India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/how-4g-changed-india) — 2023-12-02
  The 2016 data disruption did not just make the internet cheaper. It rewired what India could become.

- [What Good Policy Actually Looks Like](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/what-good-policy-actually-looks-like) — 2023-09-11
  Good policy is not the smartest analysis. It is the analysis that gets executed well enough to change outcomes for actual people.

- [Why India's Scale Matters](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/why-indias-scale-matters) — 2023-06-16
  When a country of 1.4 billion people solves a problem, the solution tends to be unusually robust. And unusually relevant.

- [Why Infrastructure Matters More Than Headlines](https://www.manasmajhi.com/india/why-infrastructure-matters-more-than-headlines) — 2023-04-29
  The stories that make news are almost always the surface layer. The real story is the infrastructure underneath that made them possible.

## Odisha (35 essays)

- [Salt, Steel, and Silicon](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/salt-steel-and-silicon) — 2026-07-06
  Three ages. Three resources. One coast, one mountain range, one generation. Odisha has had what the world needed every time the world changed what it needed. The first two ages were defined by what the land contained. The third will be defined by what the people decide.

- [Agriculture Beyond Subsidies](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/agriculture-beyond-subsidies) — 2026-07-04
  Odisha has subsidized its farmers for three decades. Farm incomes remain among the lowest in India. The problem was never a lack of support — it was the wrong kind of support. Subsidies preserve the status quo. Infrastructure changes it.

- [Water as Odisha's Strategic Asset](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/water-odishas-strategic-asset) — 2026-07-04
  Odisha has more river systems, more rainfall, and more coastline than most Indian states. It also floods regularly, irrigates less farmland than the national average, and watched Chhattisgarh build upstream dams on its primary river while it was still deciding what to do about it. This is not a geography problem.

- [The Odyssey of Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/the-odyssey-of-odisha) — 2026-06-29
  If you grew up in Odisha, you know someone who left. Maybe it was you. What it means to love a place that made you leave — and whether that is beginning to change.

- [Paradip: The Port Odisha Has Not Captured](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/paradip-port) — 2026-06-22
  Paradip Port is India's largest port by cargo volume, handling over 150 million metric tonnes annually. It sits on Odisha's coastline, routing the state's mineral wealth to the world. And yet Odisha remains one of India's least economically developed states. That gap between what Paradip handles and what Odisha captures is the central strategic question of Odisha's economic future.

- [The Odisha Skill Premium](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/the-odisha-skill-premium) — 2026-06-20
  In Tirupur, Tamil Nadu, textile employers are paying a wage premium for workers trained in Odisha. Not as policy. Because the quality is better. That fact, sitting quietly in a textile cluster 1,500 kilometres from Bhubaneswar, is worth spending some time with.

- [How Odisha Has Changed in the Last Twenty Years](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/how-odisha-has-changed) — 2026-06-16
  When I was starting my first venture I was running it through VSAT because nothing else reached Junagarh. JioFiber is there now. That compression tells you most of what you need to know about what changed — and what hasn't.

- [What Odisha Loses When Its Graduates Leave](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/what-odisha-loses-when-its-graduates-leave) — 2026-06-15
  Every year, Odisha educates tens of thousands of engineers, doctors, and managers at public expense — and then transfers most of that investment to Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Pune. The scale of this transfer is larger than most people realize.

- [Why Is Odisha Underrated?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/why-is-odisha-underrated) — 2026-01-25
  Odisha is systematically underestimated — not because it lacks substance, but because it lacks the visibility infrastructure that translates substance into perception. The gap between what the state is and what most people believe about it is large and narrowing.

- [What Industries Are Growing in Odisha?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/what-industries-are-growing-in-odisha) — 2026-01-11
  Odisha's growth story is broader than most people know. Steel and mining remain dominant, but technology, pharmaceuticals, ports and logistics, renewable energy, and tourism are all expanding in ways that are beginning to reshape the state's economic profile.

- [Why Should Companies Hire From Odisha?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/why-should-companies-hire-from-odisha) — 2026-01-04
  Odisha produces engineering and professional talent that is capable, underpriced relative to its quality, and motivated in ways that talent from saturated markets often isn't. Most companies haven't found it yet. That's the opportunity.

- [What Is the Future of Bhubaneswar?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/what-is-the-future-of-bhubaneswar) — 2025-12-14
  Bhubaneswar is at an inflection point. The decisions being made now — about talent, capital, infrastructure, and the companies that choose to build here — will determine whether it becomes a genuinely compounding city or a city that always seemed about to become something more.

- [Why Odisha Matters](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/why-odisha-matters) — 2025-10-05
  Odisha is not an afterthought in India's story. It is one of the original chapters. Understanding why it matters — historically, economically, and now — requires looking at the state on its own terms rather than through the lens of what it's not yet.

- [Beyond GDP: What a Developed Odisha Must Be Answerable For](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/beyond-gdp-what-a-developed-odisha-must-be-answerable-for) — 2025-09-29
  Economic growth is necessary for development. But it is not a definition of it. Odisha has been growing. The harder question is what that growth has actually built.

- [Odisha Economy — Current State and Trajectory](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-economy) — 2025-09-28
  Odisha has grown faster than the national average for a decade, and most of India hasn't noticed. That gap between performance and perception is itself worth examining — it says something about how economic narratives form, and who gets credit for growth they've already delivered.

- [Odisha Talent — What the State Produces](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-talent) — 2025-09-21
  Odisha produces more technical and professional talent than its local economy currently absorbs. The result is a diaspora distributed across Indian and global organisations — and a sourcing opportunity for companies willing to look.

- [Odisha Startups — Who Is Building Here](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-startups) — 2025-09-14
  Odisha's startup ecosystem is early-stage, and comparing it to Bangalore misses the point. What's worth watching is not whether it catches up to established hubs — it's whether it develops the founding conditions that produce companies the major hubs wouldn't produce.

- [Odisha Infrastructure — The Foundation Being Built](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-infrastructure) — 2025-09-07
  Odisha's infrastructure has improved faster than the state's reputation has. The mismatch between what exists on the ground and what most people believe about the state is not an accident — it is a narrative set decades ago that hasn't been updated.

- [Odisha Technology Ecosystem](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-technology-ecosystem) — 2025-08-31
  Odisha has a technology sector most people outside the state have never heard of. The question is not whether it exists — it does — but whether the conditions are in place to retain the talent it produces, rather than exporting it to cities that will build with it instead.

- [Odisha AI Ecosystem — Where It Stands and Where It's Going](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-ai-ecosystem) — 2025-08-24
  Odisha is not yet in the conversation about India's AI ecosystem. It should be. The inputs are strong — technical talent, cost structure, government intent, institutional density. What's missing is capital, senior AI talent, and a visible first win.

- [Odisha Manufacturing: India's Industrial Base](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-manufacturing) — 2025-08-17
  Odisha is one of India's most significant manufacturing states, and most people outside the industry don't know it. Steel, aluminium, chemicals, fertilisers, and a growing petrochemical corridor. This is the industrial base that funds everything else.

- [Odisha Tourism — The Most Underused Asset](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-tourism) — 2025-08-10
  Odisha has a concentration of temples, wildlife, tribal culture, and coastline that should make it one of India's premier tourism destinations. It isn't, yet. The reasons are fixable. And the trajectory is changing.

- [Why Global Companies Should Consider Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/why-global-companies-should-consider-odisha) — 2025-07-20
  The case for Odisha as a business destination goes beyond cost arbitrage. It's about access to minerals, port infrastructure, a large and underutilised talent pool, and a government that is actively competing for investment. Here is the full case.

- [Odisha Is Building the Wrong Transport System](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odisha-transport-vision) — 2025-07-14
  The debate in Odisha is Metro vs MRTS. That is the wrong question. The right question is: what transport system does a multi-city $500 billion economy actually need?

- [The Biopharma Gap Eastern India Hasn't Noticed](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/eastern-indias-biopharma-gap) — 2025-06-09
  India has world-class pharmaceutical clusters in Hyderabad, Pune, and Ahmedabad. Eastern India has none. That gap is also an opening — and Odisha is positioned to claim it.

- [What Kalinga Knew About the Indian Ocean](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/what-kalinga-knew-about-the-indian-ocean) — 2025-05-27
  Two thousand years ago, Kalinga controlled Indian Ocean trade from the eastern coast of India. The geography that made that possible has not changed. What we have done with it has.

- [Odisha's Resource Trap](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odishas-resource-trap) — 2025-05-17
  More than 30% of Odisha's SGDP comes from mines and minerals. When the reserves run out — and they will — what exactly are we leaving behind?

- [Bhubaneswar: Can It Become an AI City?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/bhubaneswar) — 2025-03-14
  Bhubaneswar has the talent pipeline, the cost structure, and the infrastructure foundation. The question is whether it can generate the ecosystem gravity that converts those inputs into an AI city.

- [Odisha's Untapped Potential](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/odishas-untapped-potential) — 2024-06-24
  The state I grew up in has more going for it than most people realize — and a widening gap between what it is and what it could be.

- [The Future of Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/the-future-of-odisha) — 2024-06-14
  Odisha has the inputs for a different trajectory. Whether it takes that trajectory is a question of policy, investment, and will.

- [A Love Letter to Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/a-love-letter-to-odisha) — 2024-02-29
  The state I grew up in shaped how I think about ambition, possibility, and the gap between potential and outcome.

- [Building a Global Business from Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/building-a-global-business-from-odisha) — 2023-09-08
  The geography of where you start is more arbitrary than you think. And less limiting than people told me it would be.

- [What Odisha Gets Right](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/what-odisha-gets-right) — 2023-05-20
  For a state that gets most of its press coverage during disasters, there are things it is doing better than the narrative suggests.

- [Showing Friends Around Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/showing-friends-around-odisha) — 2023-01-19
  When someone from outside sees your home for the first time, you see it differently too.

- [Why I Keep Talking About Odisha](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odisha/why-i-keep-talking-about-odisha) — 2022-05-30
  People sometimes ask why I spend so much time talking about a state most of the world cannot find on a map. The answer is about identity and responsibility.

## Kalahandi (24 essays)

- [Kalahandi Agriculture: The Water Paradox](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-agriculture) — 2026-06-21
  Kalahandi has rivers. It has rainfall. It has fertile soil. It has everything a farming region needs — except the infrastructure to turn rainfall into reliable harvests. That gap between what the land has and what the land produces is one of the most fixable problems in Indian agriculture. And one of the least fixed.

- [The Cultural Life of Kalahandi](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-culture-festivals) — 2026-06-20
  Every account of Kalahandi leads with poverty data. What it misses is that places shaped by sustained constraint develop cultural systems — festivals, food, community structures — that places built without adversity rarely develop. The culture is not separate from the hardship. It's the response to it.

- [What Kalahandi Sits On](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-minerals) — 2026-06-19
  Kalahandi has significant mineral wealth — bauxite, iron ore, graphite, limestone. For most of its history, those minerals have left as raw material and returned as finished goods made elsewhere. The question of who benefits from a district's natural endowments is one of the oldest questions in development economics. Kalahandi is still answering it.

- [Why It Costs Rs.3,000 to Fly to Kalahandi](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-connectivity) — 2026-06-18
  The cheapest flight in India costs Rs.400. The flight to Kalahandi costs Rs.3,000. Same flight time. Seven times the price. That gap is not about aviation economics. It's about how India decides which places get to participate in the modern economy.

- [Kalahandi's History Is Not What You Think It Is](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-history) — 2026-06-17
  For most people, Kalahandi's history begins and ends with the 1985 famine. That is like knowing Britain only through the Blitz. A place is not its worst decade. Kalahandi is ancient, complex, and has been building itself — quietly — for a very long time.

- [What Nobody Tells You About Visiting Kalahandi](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-tourism) — 2026-06-16
  Odisha's most overlooked district has waterfalls, sacred hills, royal history, and tribal culture that most of India has never heard of. That invisibility is both the problem and, for now, the charm.

- [The Talent I've Watched Leave Kalahandi](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/the-talent-ive-watched-leave-kalahandi) — 2026-06-16
  The people who left were not the ones who couldn't make it. They were often the best ones. The question is what that means for the place they left — and whether the pattern is permanent.

- [What Development Actually Looks Like in Kalahandi](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/kalahandi-development-2026) — 2026-06-15
  Kalahandi has new roads, new investment, and a NITI Aayog ranking. What it does not yet have is a reason for its best people to stay.

- [The KBK Divergence: Why Kalahandi Pulls Ahead](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/the-kbk-divergence) — 2026-06-15
  Eight districts. One development label. Very different trajectories. What's happening inside the KBK region tells us something specific about what kinds of intervention work — and what doesn't.

- [What the Aspirational Districts Ranking Actually Measures](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/what-the-aspirational-districts-ranking-actually-measures) — 2026-06-15
  Kalahandi ranked #1 in Odisha for Health and Nutrition under the NITI Aayog programme. That's real. But the ranking measures speed of improvement from a low baseline — not development level. The distinction matters more than most coverage suggests.

- [What Kalahandi Taught Me About Opportunity](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/what-kalahandi-taught-me-about-opportunity) — 2026-05-29
  Opportunity is not a place or a thing. It is a condition. Kalahandi made that visible before I had the language for it.

- [The Childhood Lessons I Still Use Every Day](https://www.manasmajhi.com/kalahandi/the-childhood-lessons-i-still-use-every-day) — 2026-05-18
  Most of the lessons that actually run my life came from growing up in Kalahandi, not from any formal education or professional experience that followed.

## Hiring (32 essays)

- [Measuring Executive Hiring Reliability](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/executive-hiring-reliability-report) — 2026-06-29
  40–50% of executive hires fail within 18 months. The industry has accepted this as a market condition rather than a methodology failure. It is a methodology failure. Reliability in executive search is not an accident — it is the product of specific process decisions that most search firms do not make.

- [The Cost of a Failed Executive Search](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/the-cost-of-a-failed-executive-hire) — 2026-06-29
  The objection to retained executive search is almost always framed as a fee problem. The fee is not the expensive part. What happens when the search methodology fails is.

- [Where AI Actually Improves Hiring](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/where-ai-actually-improves-hiring) — 2026-06-29
  Most AI recruiting claims are marketing. A smaller set of AI applications create genuine, measurable operational improvement. The difference matters — not as a technology question but as an operations question.

- [Why Your ATS Is Not Hiring Infrastructure](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/why-ats-is-not-hiring-infrastructure) — 2026-06-29
  An ATS is a candidate database with workflow automation. Hiring infrastructure is something different — the observability, recovery, and execution layer that prevents the database from becoming a graveyard. Conflating them is why most VP searches stall.

- [Why Internal Recruiting Breaks at Executive Scale](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/why-internal-recruiting-breaks-at-executive-scale) — 2026-06-29
  Most companies have internal recruiters. Most companies still fail at executive hiring. These two facts are not in tension — they follow directly from how internal recruiting functions are built, what they are optimized for, and where that optimization stops working.

  The most common thing I hear from hiring managers is 'we need someone exceptional.' After five years and 25+ placements, I have learned that exceptional is almost never what they mean.

- [Broken Hiring Systems and the Opportunity Gap](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/broken-hiring-systems-and-the-opportunity-gap) — 2026-06-14
  The opportunity gap is usually discussed as a problem of who gets found. The more important problem is what happens after they're found — and why the system destroys more opportunity than talent scarcity ever does.

- [CTO Recruitment in India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/cto-recruitment-india) — 2026-05-31

  The 50-day executive search is not a faster version of the standard process. It is a different architecture — one designed to eliminate the four delay patterns that make most VP and C-suite searches take 120 days. This is the process behind the 41-day close.

- [How to Write an Executive Role Brief](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/how-to-write-an-executive-role-brief) — 2026-04-29
  Most executive searches start with a job description written for LinkedIn. A role brief is a different document entirely — and the difference determines whether you find the right person.

- [How Executive Search Actually Works](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/how-executive-search-works) — 2026-04-19
  Most companies have a vague sense of what executive search involves. The reality is more structured and more consequential than most people expect — and understanding it changes how you run the process.

- [Why Executive Searches Fail](https://www.manasmajhi.com/hiring/why-executive-searches-fail) — 2026-04-12
  Most executive search failures are diagnosed at the point of failure. The actual cause is almost always upstream — in decisions made at the start of the search that made failure inevitable before outreach began.

  The executive brief is the most important document in a search. Most are vague enough to be useless. The ones that produce great shortlists share specific characteristics that can be learned and applied.

  Most companies treat retained and contingency search as two price points for the same service. They are structurally different models with different incentives — and the difference in incentives explains almost every quality gap between them.

  Across the VP-level mandates we track, 68% stall at or before week 10. The cause is almost never the talent market. It's almost always the execution layer — and whether anyone can see inside it.

  40–50% of executive hires fail within 18 months — not because the wrong person was selected, but because of three failure modes that play out after the offer is signed. They are specific, predictable, and mostly preventable.

  Moving from #87 to #18 in the World Staffing Leader rankings tells two stories. One is about a firm getting sharper. The other is about an industry where doing this work with genuine rigour still moves you up the list fast — because so few firms actually do it.

## Future of Work (26 essays)

- [The Five Capabilities Executives Will Need by 2030](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/five-capabilities-executives-need-2030) — 2026-07-10
  Leadership is no longer about having the most information. It is about designing organizations that make the best decisions. A framework grounded in 2026 research from McKinsey, Deloitte, BCG, and Microsoft.

  Most productivity advice about AI tells you what to outsource to it. That question matters, but it misses the harder one: what do you keep? The answer to that question will determine what kind of person you become over the next ten years.

- [What AI Agents Actually Are](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/what-ai-agents-actually-are) — 2026-06-30
  The term has been diluted to the point of uselessness. Here's what agents actually are, why most production deployments fail, and what the infrastructure gap looks like from the inside.

- [Why Human Judgment Still Matters in Hiring](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/why-human-judgment-still-matters-in-hiring) — 2026-06-30
  Every few years, a new tool promises to take the human bias out of hiring and replace it with something more rigorous. The tool always underperforms on the thing that matters most: predicting whether a specific person will succeed in a specific role at a specific company. Here is why that prediction remains stubbornly human.

- [The Rise of the Fractional Executive](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-rise-of-the-fractional-executive) — 2026-06-29
  The fractional executive model is growing fast, and most of the enthusiasm is justified. But the model has a structural limit that neither side talks about honestly: the things that make a leader effective at a company usually require more time than fractional allows.

- [The Global Hiring Floor](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-global-hiring-floor) — 2026-06-28
  AI is not just changing who does the work. It is changing what the work is worth. As AI tools raise the output floor for every knowledge worker, the question of what human talent commands — and why — is being rewritten in real time.

- [How Companies Should Actually Think About AI Adoption](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/how-companies-should-think-about-ai-adoption) — 2026-06-23
  88% of organisations use AI somewhere. Fewer than 40% have scaled beyond a pilot. The gap isn't technology — it's how companies frame the problem from the start.

- [What the History of Automation Actually Tells Us About AI](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/what-the-history-of-automation-tells-us-about-ai) — 2026-06-22
  The optimists cite history to argue we shouldn't worry. The pessimists cite history to argue this time is catastrophically different. Both are misreading it. The history of automation is more complicated — and more honest — than either side is willing to be.

- [AI and the Future of Talent Sourcing](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/ai-and-the-future-of-talent-sourcing) — 2026-06-17
  AI has already changed how candidates are found. What it hasn't changed — and what I believe it won't change in the foreseeable future — is how the best candidates are persuaded. The sourcing problem was never primarily about finding people. It was about reaching the right people in a way that makes them want to engage.

- [What Building Distributed Teams Actually Requires](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/building-distributed-teams) — 2026-06-16
  Distributed teams are not remote teams with better Slack. They are a fundamentally different organizational model that requires different hiring, different communication, and different leadership. Most companies that try it fail not because the model is wrong, but because they apply co-located assumptions to a distributed reality.

- [The Knowledge Problem in AI](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-knowledge-problem-in-ai) — 2026-06-16
  AI captures what was written down. The most valuable knowledge in any organisation was never written down. That gap is not a bug in the technology — it's the central challenge of deploying AI that actually works.

- [Why AI Makes Org Structure More Important](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/why-ai-makes-organisational-structure-more-important) — 2026-06-15
  The assumption is that AI flattens hierarchy and reduces the need for formal structure. The opposite is true. AI compresses execution — and when execution is no longer the bottleneck, the quality of your decision architecture becomes everything.

- [Why Every Sector Learns Observability the Hard Way](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/why-every-sector-learns-observability-the-hard-way) — 2026-04-04
  Software operations learned it after enough production outages. Finance learned it after enough risk events. Hiring hasn't learned it yet — but the lesson is coming. The only question is whether you're ready before the failure that forces it.

- [The Recruiter Isn't Being Replaced](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-recruiter-isnt-being-replaced) — 2026-03-20
  Every conversation about AI and recruiting focuses on replacement. The more accurate framing is redesign. The tactical, high-volume parts of the job are being automated. What's left is more valuable — and harder.

- [AI and Hiring — What Actually Changes](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/ai-and-hiring) — 2025-12-07
  AI is changing hiring. Most of the conversation about how is wrong. The changes that matter are not about automation replacing recruiters — they are about who wins the talent competition in a world where sourcing is commoditised.

- [AI and Education](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/ai-and-education) — 2025-11-30
  AI is not fixing the fundamental problem with education, which is not content delivery — it is access, relevance, and the signal that credentials send to employers. It is, however, creating new paths around the problem.

- [The Autonomous Hiring Era](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-autonomous-hiring-era) — 2025-11-29
  Hiring is going through the same transition that software operations went through a decade ago — from human-operated to AI-orchestrated. The companies that understand this shift will have a structural advantage. The ones that don't will wonder why their hiring keeps breaking.

- [AI and India](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/ai-and-india) — 2025-11-16
  India's relationship with AI is different from the relationship that Silicon Valley assumes. The constraints are different, the opportunities are different, and the version of AI that matters most for India is not the version that dominates the global conversation.

- [Remote Work — What We Now Know](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/remote-work-what-we-know) — 2025-11-09
  Five years of data and experience have settled some of the questions about remote work and surfaced new ones. The debate has moved from whether remote work is possible to which kinds of work it suits and which it doesn't.

- [Global Talent — How Borders Are Dissolving](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/global-talent-how-borders-are-dissolving) — 2025-11-02
  The geography of talent has dissolved faster than the geography of hiring processes. Most companies still filter candidates by zip code while the best people for the role are somewhere they've never sourced from.

- [Skills vs Degrees — The Ongoing Shift](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/skills-vs-degrees) — 2025-10-26
  The degree has not been replaced. But its dominance as a signal is eroding in specific domains, and the erosion is accelerating. Understanding where credentials still matter — and where they are being bypassed — is now a practical question for anyone building a career or a team.

- [What Makes Great Talent Stand Out](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/what-makes-great-talent-stand-out) — 2025-10-19
  The observable differences between great performers and good performers tend to accumulate in a small number of patterns. Not natural ability. Not credentials. The habits of mind and work that compound over time.

- [Why Talented People Stay Unnoticed](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/why-talented-people-stay-unnoticed) — 2025-10-12
  The most capable person in a room is not always the most visible one. Talent and visibility are different variables, determined by different things. Understanding why they diverge — and what to do about it — matters for anyone trying to build great teams or advance their own career.

- [AI and Human Potential](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/ai-and-human-potential) — 2024-07-24
  AI will either be the most powerful opportunity-expanding technology in history or the most efficient mechanism for concentrating advantage ever built. Which one it becomes depends on decisions being made right now by people who are not asking that question.

- [The Next Decade of Work](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/the-next-decade-of-work) — 2024-03-14

- [What Automation Cannot Replace](https://www.manasmajhi.com/future-of-work/what-automation-cannot-replace) — 2024-01-26
  Not everything that seems replaceable is. The answer turns out to be less about complexity and more about something else.

## Entrepreneurship (13 essays)

- [How Incentive Systems Shape Culture](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/how-incentive-systems-shape-culture) — 2026-06-30
  Every organisation has a stated culture and a real culture. The gap between them is not a communication problem. It is an incentive design problem. What you reward is what you get — regardless of what you say you value.

- [How to Build a Culture That Doesn't Depend on You](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/how-to-build-a-culture-that-doesnt-depend-on-you) — 2026-06-30
  The cultures of founder-led companies feel coherent while the founder is present. Most of them don't survive the founder's departure — or even the founder's distraction. The culture wasn't built. It was performed.

- [How to Design Systems That Outlast Their Designers](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/how-to-design-systems-that-outlast-their-designers) — 2026-06-30
  The hardest design problem is not making something work. It is making something work after the people who built it are no longer there to interpret it. That is a different problem, and almost nobody is taught how to solve it.

- [The Accountability Architecture Problem](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/the-accountability-architecture-problem) — 2026-06-30
  Most organisations have responsibility without accountability. The two sound the same and produce completely different behaviour. One is assigned. The other is real.

- [The Decision Architecture That Scales](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/the-decision-architecture-that-scales) — 2026-06-30
  Every founder reaches the same wall: the organisation can only move as fast as they can personally decide. The answer is not to work harder. It is to design a decision system that doesn't require you at every node.

- [What Makes Institutions Endure While Companies Don't](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/what-makes-institutions-endure) — 2026-06-30
  The average S&P 500 company lifespan has fallen from 61 years in 1958 to under 18 years today. Most companies are built to grow. Very few are designed to last. The difference is not strategy — it's architecture.

- [Why Most Organisations Fail to Learn](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/why-most-organisations-fail-to-learn) — 2026-06-30
  Individual learning is difficult. Organisational learning is harder by an order of magnitude — because organisations don't learn the way people do. They need infrastructure to learn at all. Most never build it.

- [From Service to System](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/from-service-to-system) — 2026-06-27
  The hardest transition in a service business is not from zero to one client. It's from delivering to ten clients by running harder, to delivering to fifty clients because you've built something that scales. One is hustle. The other is architecture. Most founders figure this out only after the hustle stops working.

- [Why Cold Outreach Is a Founder's Most Underrated Skill](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/why-cold-outreach-is-a-founders-most-underrated-skill) — 2026-06-25
  Most founders treat cold outreach as a necessary evil — something to survive until referrals take over. I think that's exactly backwards. Cold outreach is a discipline that, done well, compounds faster than almost anything else a founder can build.

- [The Advantage of Building Outside the Metro](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/the-advantage-of-building-outside-the-metro) — 2026-06-23
  Everyone told me to move to Bangalore. I didn't. What I learned from building in Odisha is that the cost of not being in a hub is mostly overstated, and the benefits are almost never talked about.

- [What Kind of Institution Are You Building?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/what-am-i-building) — 2024-05-08
  Most founders answer 'what are you building?' with a product description. The deeper question — what kind of institution are you building — gets deferred until it's too late to design the answer deliberately.

- [Building as a Response to a Place](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/why-i-build) — 2024-01-27
  The mission of an institution is shaped by the problem it came from. Kalahandi taught me something specific about gaps between what exists and what's possible — and building has been my answer to that ever since.

- [Building Through Uncertainty](https://www.manasmajhi.com/entrepreneurship/building-through-uncertainty) — 2022-03-22
  The founders who last are not the ones who had certainty. They are the ones who learned to make good decisions without it.

## Philosophy (24 essays)

- [A World of Eight Billion Typists](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/a-world-of-eight-billion-typists) — 2026-06-17

  A set of beliefs about how the world works, accumulated from a specific life in specific places. Not a philosophy. A working model — held with conviction but open to revision when the evidence demands it.

- [How I Think About Learning](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/how-i-think-about-learning) — 2024-12-22
  Learning is not a passive accumulation of information. It is an active process of updating models — and the models you hold determine which new information you can absorb and which you can't. Understanding this changes how you learn.

- [How I Think About Systems](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/how-i-think-about-systems) — 2024-12-15
  A system is any set of components that interact to produce an output. The output is almost never what any individual component intended. This is why fixing individual components rarely fixes the output — and why thinking in systems is a different kind of intelligence than thinking about things in isolation.

- [How I Think About People](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/how-i-think-about-people) — 2024-12-08
  After five years of evaluating people for the highest-stakes roles in organisations, and a life before that of paying close attention to how people actually behave versus how they say they will, a few durable observations have accumulated.

- [Books That Changed My Thinking](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/books-that-changed-my-thinking) — 2024-12-01
  Not a reading list. A list of the specific books that actually changed something in how I think — what the change was, and why it happened then rather than earlier or later.

- [Questions I Keep Returning To](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/questions-i-keep-returning-to) — 2024-11-24
  The questions that are most worth asking don't resolve. They clarify — they generate better understanding without producing a final answer. These are the ones I keep coming back to.

- [On Identity and Where You Come From](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/on-identity-and-where-you-come-from) — 2024-11-17
  Where you come from shapes how you see without you choosing it. The question is not whether this is true — it is — but what to do with it: what to carry, what to question, and how to hold both without losing either.

- [On Success: What It Actually Means](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/on-success-what-it-actually-means) — 2024-11-10
  Success is a word that carries a lot of freight and is used to mean very different things. Getting clear on what you actually mean by it — not what the ambient culture means — turns out to be one of the more important pieces of work a person can do.

- [Learning From People](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/learning-from-people) — 2024-08-14
  The most underrated form of education is the one that happens in conversation — and most of us are not paying enough attention.

- [What Changed My Mind This Year?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/what-changed-my-mind-this-year) — 2024-08-03
  Updating your beliefs is not a sign of weakness. It is what careful thinking looks like over time.

- [What Am I Learning?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/what-am-i-learning) — 2024-06-21
  The most important learning does not announce itself. It accumulates in the gaps between what you expected and what you found.

- [The Evolution of My Thinking](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/the-evolution-of-my-thinking) — 2023-05-11
  The beliefs worth holding are the ones that survive contact with new evidence. Most of mine have changed at least once.

- [How to Make Decisions When You Don't Have Enough Information](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/decisions-under-uncertainty) — 2023-05-08
  Most important decisions are made under uncertainty. The question is not how to eliminate uncertainty before deciding — it is how to decide well despite it.

- [What Failure Actually Teaches](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/what-failure-teaches) — 2023-02-20
  Failure teaches things that success cannot. The question is whether you are paying enough attention to extract what it is offering.

- [People Are More Similar Than Different](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/people-are-more-similar-than-different) — 2023-01-17
  The surface differences are real. The depth of similarity underneath them is consistently surprising.

- [Luck vs. Preparation: What Actually Determines Outcomes](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/luck-vs-preparation) — 2022-11-14
  The debate about whether success comes from luck or preparation usually misses the more interesting question: how preparation changes the distribution of outcomes over time.

- [Midnight Calls and Invisible Sacrifices](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/midnight-calls-and-invisible-sacrifices) — 2022-08-18
  The version of work that the world sees is never the whole version. What stays invisible is usually the part that costs the most.

- [Long-Term Thinking in a Short-Term World](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/long-term-thinking-in-a-short-term-world) — 2022-08-01
  The advantages of thinking long are real and underutilized. The difficulty is that almost everything in the environment is pushing the other way.

- [Have They Done This Before?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/have-they-done-this-before) — 2022-05-13
  Past experience is a reasonable signal. The question is which experience actually predicts what you need.

- [Contentment vs. Success](https://www.manasmajhi.com/philosophy/contentment-vs-success) — 2022-03-26
  The tension between the two is real. But the framing that treats them as opposites misses something important.

## Travel (13 essays)

- [When Generosity Is the Default](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/kazakhstan-generosity) — 2026-06-15
  Most environments run on friction as their baseline. Almaty ran differently. What a midnight flight out of Kazakhstan revealed about how environment shapes behaviour — and what that means for everything you're trying to build.

- [The Edited Version of Yourself](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/phi-phi-being-seen) — 2026-06-15
  Most people carry a conservative self-image built from accumulated evidence. The people who change your trajectory are the ones who refuse your edited version. Six days on Phi Phi Island, and a woman who saw something before I did.

- [What Travel Has Taught Me](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/what-travel-has-taught-me) — 2025-02-09
  Travel doesn't primarily teach tolerance or perspective or humility — that's what travel writing claims. What it actually teaches is more specific: that most of the certainties you carry about how the world works were assembled from a very small sample.

- [Places That Changed How I Think](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/places-that-changed-how-i-think) — 2025-02-02
  Not every place you visit changes anything. A few do — not because of what they look like but because of what they make visible that was invisible before. These are the ones that changed something specific.

- [What Home Looks Like From Far Away](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/what-home-looks-like-from-far-away) — 2025-01-26
  Distance clarifies things that proximity obscures. The place you grew up looks different from London than from Bhawanipatna. Not because it has changed — because you have a reference point now, and the reference point changes everything you see.

- [Travel as a Learning System](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/travel-as-a-learning-system) — 2025-01-19
  Most people treat travel as consumption — experiences to accumulate, places to check off. The people who extract the most from it treat it as a system: deliberate inputs, structured observation, intentional extraction of what is transferable. The difference in output is large.

- [What Does Travel Teach You About Yourself?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/what-does-travel-teach-you-about-yourself) — 2025-01-12
  Travel doesn't reveal a hidden self. It creates conditions under which the self you already have becomes more visible — by removing the context that usually explains your behaviour and leaving only you.

- [Why Frequent Travelers Think Differently](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/why-frequent-travelers-think-differently) — 2025-01-05
  The frequent traveler's advantage is not knowledge of geography or cultural trivia. It is a specific set of cognitive habits — built by repeated exposure to environments where your default mental models don't work — that transfer into almost every domain of consequential work.

- [What Travel Teaches Us About Home](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/what-travel-teaches-us-about-home) — 2024-11-25
  You cannot see where you are from until you have been somewhere else — and the seeing changes everything.

- [Langkawi: The Day Everything Looked Perfect](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/langkawi-the-day-everything-looked-perfect) — 2023-09-26
  There are places that produce a specific clarity. Langkawi was one of them, on a day when I needed it.

- [Lessons from Airports](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/lessons-from-airports) — 2023-04-06
  Airports are designed to make time disappear. What they actually do is remove every distraction you normally use to avoid thinking. I've had more useful conversations and clearer thoughts in airports than in most offices. The environment people most want to escape might be the one most worth paying attention to.

- [Stories from the Road](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/stories-from-the-road) — 2022-07-19
  The stories worth keeping from years of travel are not the destinations. They are the unexpected conversations in between.

- [Why Food Matters More Than We Think](https://www.manasmajhi.com/travel/why-food-matters-more-than-we-think) — 2022-05-07
  Food is how a place explains itself to strangers. Pay attention and you learn things the guidebooks miss.

## Frameworks (11 essays)

- [Geography Advantage Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/geography-advantage-framework) — 2026-06-12
  Where you build shapes what you can build. Geography is not just a cost variable or a constraint — it is a strategic input that creates specific, compounding advantages when chosen deliberately.

- [First-Generation Founder Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/first-generation-founder-framework) — 2026-06-07
  First-generation founders carry specific advantages that consensus startup culture doesn't recognise — and specific blind spots that it doesn't warn them about. This framework maps both.

- [Talent Signal Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/talent-signal-framework) — 2025-06-13
  Most hiring processes test for proxies — credentials, presentation, pedigree. Genuine talent has different signals. This framework maps what those signals are and how to surface them.

- [Hiring SLO Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/hiring-slo-framework) — 2025-06-06
  In engineering, a service level objective defines acceptable performance thresholds and triggers automated responses when breached. Most hiring teams have no equivalent. That is the gap this framework closes.

- [Compounding Failure Loop™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/compounding-failure-loop) — 2025-05-30
  When a mandate fails, the natural response is to add more inputs. This usually makes things worse. What looks like a sourcing problem is almost always a symptom of a failure that started several stages earlier.

- [Failure Prediction System™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/failure-prediction-system) — 2025-05-23
  Mandate failure is not sudden. It is telegraphed, weeks in advance, through five consistent signals. Most teams don't monitor them until after the damage is done.

- [Mandate Recovery Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/mandate-recovery-framework) — 2025-05-16
  When a VP search stalls, the default response is to add more: more sourcing, more outreach, a new vendor. These are supply-side solutions to a demand-side problem. Recovery requires a different sequence.

- [Opportunity Mobility Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/opportunity-mobility-framework) — 2025-05-09
  Opportunity alone is not enough. The question is whether individuals can convert opportunity into actual mobility. Most systemic interventions fail because they solve for opportunity without solving for the conditions that make mobility real.

- [Hiring System Health™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/hiring-system-health) — 2025-05-02
  A hiring mandate is a system. Like all systems, it has health metrics. Most organisations measure outcomes — did we hire? — instead of health — is the system working? By the time outcomes fail, it's too late.

- [Intelligence Hiring System™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/intelligence-hiring-system) — 2025-04-25
  Most hiring fails not because of bad candidates but because of bad intelligence. Three layers, working in sequence. Without all three, decisions are guesses dressed as judgement.

- [Opportunity Framework™](https://www.manasmajhi.com/frameworks/opportunity-framework) — 2025-04-18
  Opportunity is not a single event. It is a chain — five links, each enabling the next. Understanding where chains break is how you design systems that close the gap between talent and potential.

## ଓଡ଼ିଆ (Odia) (3 essays)

- [ଆମ ପାଳି](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odia/ama-pali) — 2026-07-10
  ଆଜି ଇତିହାସ ଆମକୁ ପଚାରୁନାହିଁ — ତୁମେ କେତେ ବଡ଼ ହେବ, ତୁମେ କେତେ ପ୍ରସିଦ୍ଧ ହେବ। ସେ କେବଳ ଗୋଟିଏ କଥା ପଚାରୁଛି — ତୁମେ ତୁମ ଅଂଶଟି ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ କରିବ କି?

- [ବିକାଶର ରଥ](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odia/bikashar-ratha) — 2026-07-02
  ରଥଯାତ୍ରାରେ ଯେମିତି ଲକ୍ଷ ଲକ୍ଷ ହାତ ଗୋଟିଏ ରଶି ଧରନ୍ତି, ସେମିତି ବିକଶିତ ଓଡ଼ିଶା ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଓଡ଼ିଆଙ୍କ ଦ୍ୱାରା ଗଢ଼ି ଉଠିବ। ଏ ରଶି ପଚାରେ ନାହିଁ — ତୁମେ କିଏ। ଏ ଗୋଟିଏ ହିଁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ପଚାରେ — ତୁମେ ଟାଣିବ କି?

- [ଓଡ଼ିଶା ପାଇଁ ଆପଣଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱପ୍ନ କ'ଣ?](https://www.manasmajhi.com/odia/odisha-pai-apanka-swapna) — 2026-07-02
  ସ୍ୱପ୍ନ ଦେଖିବା ସହଜ। ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବା କଷ୍ଟକର। ଆମ ପିଢ଼ି ସମ୍ମୁଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଠିଆ ହୋଇଛି — ଆମେ କ'ଣ ଏକ ବିକଶିତ ଓଡ଼ିଶା ଗଢ଼ିପାରିବା? ବିକଶିତ ଓଡ଼ିଶା ସରକାରଙ୍କ ପ୍ରକଳ୍ପ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହା ସାଢ଼େ ଚାରି କୋଟି ଓଡ଼ିଆଙ୍କର ସାମୂହିକ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ।
